# Module 8: Post Classification Analysis: Change Detection {#sec-module-8-change}

## Module Overview

This module extends the post-classification and synthesis framework of
the Luma platform to support multitemporal land use and land cover
(LULC) dynamics across two or more observation periods
($T_1, T_2, \dots, T_N$). In standard single-map operations, Module 8
produces the Map Creation and Quality Report for an individual map
identity. This change analysis extension activates when a project
contains two or more classified LULC maps generated under a shared,
harmonized classification scheme from [Module 6](@sec-module-6).

This experimental implementation compares classified maps across
observation periods, summarises mapped transitions and class-level
dynamics, presents straightforward charts, and generates a land use and
land cover map change analysis report. Change analysis runs without a
trajectory table. Trajectory interpretation may be added as a possible
further extension.

## Delivery sequence {.unnumbered}

The change-analysis approach builds on the [LUMENS Pre-QuES
module](https://github.com/icraf-indonesia/lumens-shiny/). This
reference adapts the primary functionalities to the Luma workflow.

- **LULC change analysis:** compare a selected map pair; calculate
  mapped transition areas, the full transition matrix, per-class
  dynamics, and the largest off-diagonal transitions; show a horizontal
  bar chart and a multi-epoch stacked composition chart; export a report
  and tables.

- **Possible further extension:** optional trajectory mapping, analysis
  by planning unit, and additional visualisations. Trajectory mapping
  would allow users to group transitions under meaningful names. These
  additions require separate design decisions and are not prerequisites
  for change analysis.

## Input {.unnumbered}

**User Input**

1.  Selection of the comparison pair: baseline epoch ($T_a$) and
    comparison epoch ($T_b$). Other available epochs may be displayed in
    the composition chart.
2.  Specification of change direction: chronological ($T_a \to T_b$) or
    retrospective ($T_b \to T_a$).
3.  Export destination and asset format: browser direct download where
    Earth Engine limits permit, cloud delivery to Google Drive, or
    materialization as a permanent Google Earth Engine asset.
4.  **Possible further extension:** an optional user-defined trajectory
    mapping, entered directly or supplied from a reusable file. An
    absent mapping does not block change analysis.

**Automatic System Input**

1.  Project Map Registry: catalogue of all classified LULC maps
    generated within the project, including acquisition timestamps,
    sensor identifiers, spatial bounding boundaries, and model
    parameters.
2.  Geometric boundary of the Area of Interest (AOI) from [Module
    1](@sec-module-1).
3.  Harmonized LULC classification scheme with $K$ classes from [Module
    2](@sec-module-2).

**Input from Other Modules**

1.  Classified raster map for epoch $T_a$ with model metadata from
    [Module 6](@sec-module-6) and accuracy assessment from [Module
    7](@sec-module-7) (if evaluated).
2.  Classified raster map for epoch $T_b$ with model metadata from
    [Module 6](@sec-module-6).
3.  Minimum-cloud composite parameters, sensor metadata, and date
    parsing records from [Module 1](@sec-module-1).

## Output {.unnumbered}

1.  **Mapped LULC Change Layer**: the classified map pair and its mapped
    transitions. A trajectory layer would be produced only if the
    optional extension is used.
2.  **LULC Transition Matrix**: a square $K \times K$ cross-tabulation
    matrix reporting transition area in both absolute hectares ($ha$)
    and proportional landscape percentage ($\%$).
3.  **Landscape Dynamics Summary Table**: per-class metrics capturing
    initial area ($A_1$), final area ($A_2$), persistence ($P_k$), gross
    loss ($L_k$), gross gain ($G_k$), net change ($N_k$), and annualized
    rate of change ($r$).
4.  **Top 10 Dominant Transitions Table and Chart**: isolates and ranks
    the ten largest class-to-class transitions ($T_a \to T_b$) by area
    in hectares ($ha$) and proportional share ($\%$) of total change,
    drawing on the LUMENS Pre-QuES approach.
5.  **Landscape Composition Chart**: stacked bars comparing class areas
    across available epochs ($T_1, T_2, \dots, T_N$); a stacked area
    view may be offered when three or more comparable epochs are
    available.
6.  **Land Use and Land Cover Map Change Analysis Report**: a report
    with the analysis identity, mapped results, limitations, and charts.
    A trajectory section would appear only if the optional extension has
    been run.
7.  **Multitemporal Export Bundle**: change tables, the report, and
    requested map outputs. Trajectory outputs would be included only if
    the optional extension has been run.

## Checking Multitemporal Prerequisites {#sec-module-8-change-prerequisites}

This is part of **System Response 8.1: Check Multitemporal Inputs**.
Luma-GE checks the Project Map Registry when the user opens Tab 2.

::: callout-important
## Error Handling Notification: Minimum Map Requirement

Module 8's Tab 2 (LULC Change Analysis) cannot be accessed if fewer than
two classified LULC maps have been produced by [Module
6](@sec-module-6). If only a single map exists, Tab 2 remains disabled
and displays this notification:

*"Change analysis requires at least two classified LULC maps. Classify
an additional observation period in Module 6 to unlock multitemporal
analysis."*
:::

If at least two classified maps are available, Tab 2 enables pair
selection. Otherwise, the interface remains in single-map review mode
(Tab 1).

## Selecting the Comparison Pair {#sec-select-comparison-pair}

This is part of **User Journey 8.2: Select Maps and Comparison**. The
user selects the two classified maps and the direction of comparison,
then starts the analysis. Other available maps may contribute to the
composition chart. If Luma-GE identifies an incompatibility, the
interface shows the issue so the user can correct the selection or the
source maps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Multitemporal Data Collection and Verification {#sec-change-data-collection}

This is part of **System Response 8.1: Check Multitemporal Inputs**.
Luma-GE verifies the selected pair before calculating mapped change.

1.  **Map comparability**: Check that the selected maps use consistent
    class definitions, compatible spatial grids, and comparable
    observation periods. Record relevant differences in sensor,
    acquisition conditions, and processing inherited from upstream
    modules. Differences that would change the meaning of a transition
    require correction or a clear warning before analysis.
2.  **Common analysis area**: Compare only locations with valid class
    values in both maps within the selected AOI. Record the area
    included and excluded by this rule. Any spatial alignment or
    resampling applied during comparison must be documented.

::: callout-tip
## Related Function

`change_detection.LULCChangeDetector.validate_multitemporal_inputs()`:
checks CRS, pixel grid alignment, bounding geometry intersection, and
legend consistency across the input map pair.
:::

## Upstream Integration across Modules 1 to 7 {#sec-upstream-alignment}

Multitemporal change detection relies on upstream modules operating
under an integrated contract:

### Module 1: Multitemporal Image Acquisition & Seasonal Alignment

1.  **Mapping Mode**: In multitemporal mode, Module 1 accepts an array
    of target dates: `[T_1, T_2, ..., T_N]`.
2.  **Date Range Interpretation**:
    - When the user specifies a 4-digit year (e.g. `2020` and `2023`),
      `data_acquisition.parse_date_input()` interprets the range as
      January 1 to December 31 for each year. Both composites encompass
      a full 12-month annual cycle, where statistical median aggregation
      naturally dampens seasonal phenological fluctuations.
    - When the user specifies a custom sub-annual date range (e.g.
      `2020-06-01` to `2020-09-30`, representing a dry season), the
      system enforces the same calendar month and day boundaries for
      comparison years (`2023-06-01` to `2023-09-30`) to reduce
      differences caused by seasonal vegetation conditions.
3.  **Sensor Comparability**:
    - **Related sensors**: Calibrated products from closely related
      sensors, such as Landsat 8 and Landsat 9, improve consistency but
      do not remove the need to check product versions, observation
      conditions, and map quality across periods. [USGS Landsat 8–9
      Surface Reflectance quality
      assessment](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-8-9-surface-reflectance-quality-assessment).
    - **Different sensors**: Differences in spectral response,
      resolution, processing, and acquisition conditions can affect the
      classified maps. Document how the inputs were made comparable and
      flag remaining uncertainty. Harmonised products may help where
      appropriate. [NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2
      product](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/NASA_HLS_HLSL30_v002).

### Module 2: Classification Scheme

Establishes a single project-wide classification scheme with $K$ classes
applied across all observation periods.

### Module 3: Sample Data Preparation with Image Composite Attribution

1.  The user uploads or digitizes ground reference samples.
2.  **Temporal Association**: The user explicitly assigns the sample
    dataset to its corresponding image composite: *"Select the composite
    that matches this training dataset: \[Composite T1 \| Composite T2
    \| ... \| Composite Tn\]"*. This anchors the reference ground truth
    to its authentic observation date ($C_{selected}$).

### Module 4: Sample Data Quality Analysis

Executes Transformed Divergence (TD) spectral separability testing
specifically between the training sample data and its designated
matching composite ($C_{selected}$).

### Module 5: Predictor Variables

Applies an identical, symmetric predictor pipeline (spectral bands,
indices such as NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, and terrain variables) across all
composites ($C_1, C_2, \dots, C_N$), ensuring uniform feature space
dimensionality.

### Module 6: Model Training & Multitemporal Inference

1.  **Model Calibration**: The Random Forest classifier is trained on
    the specified pair: `(Training Data, Composite C_selected)`. Model
    accuracy (stratified split confusion matrix) is evaluated on the
    validation split for that epoch.
2.  **Direct Spectral Transfer**: The trained classifier is applied
    directly to infer LULC maps across all composites in the project
    ($T_1, T_2, \dots, T_N$), populating the Project Map Registry.
    - **Assumptions**: Surface reflectance processing and comparable
      seasonal windows reduce some differences between observations but
      do not guarantee that class signatures remain stable across dates.
    - **Advantages**: Requires zero additional field data collection for
      comparison years; rapid execution; consistent classification
      logic.
    - **Limitations**: Inter-annual precipitation differences, sensor
      degradation, and vegetation phenology can induce spectral drift,
      resulting in false-positive class transitions.
    - **Future Improvement Roadmap**: Planned implementation of
      *Pseudo-invariant Sample Extraction (PISE)* to automatically
      identify statistically stable pixels between $C_1$ and $C_2$,
      generating retrained temporal classifiers without new field
      campaigns.

### Module 7: Map Accuracy Assessment

The user selects which predicted map ($T_1$ or $T_2$) to independently
validate using available ground reference validation samples.

## Server-Side Spatial Transition Computation {#sec-compute-transitions}

This is part of **System Response 8.2: Calculate Mapped Change**.

To prevent client memory overloads, all spatial cross-tabulations
execute server-side in Google Earth Engine.

1.  **Pixel Combination Formulation**: For non-negative integer class
    codes $i$ and $j$, select and record a multiplier $M$ greater than
    the largest class code in the harmonised scheme. Then
    $$\text{Transition\_Code} = T_a \times M + T_b$$ gives each ordered
    class pair a unique code. Validate the class-code range before
    computation; the value 100 is suitable only when every class code is
    below 100. In Earth Engine:

    ``` python
    transition_image = image_ta.multiply(multiplier).add(image_tb).rename("transition_code")
    ```

2.  **Server-Side Transition Area Reduction**: Apply a shared
    valid-pixel mask to both classified maps and aggregate
    `ee.Image.pixelArea()` by transition code over the AOI, using an
    explicit analysis projection and scale. This returns mapped area in
    square metres for each observed transition. Record the selected
    grid, scale, mask rule, and covered area.

3.  **Tabular Matrix Compilation**: Convert each summed transition area
    from square metres to hectares:
    $p_{ij} = \text{Area}_{ij,m^2}/10{,}000$. Pixel frequency may be
    retained as a diagnostic, but a fixed count multiplied by nominal
    scale squared is not the area estimator.

4.  **Landscape Dynamics Formulation**:

    - **Initial Area (**$A_1$): $A_{1i} = \sum_{j=1}^K p_{ij}$
    - **Final Area (**$A_2$): $A_{2j} = \sum_{i=1}^K p_{ij}$
    - **Persistence (**$P_k$): $p_{kk}$ (diagonal entries)
    - **Gross Loss (**$L_k$): $A_{1k} - p_{kk} = \sum_{j \ne k} p_{kj}$
    - **Gross Gain (**$G_k$): $A_{2k} - p_{kk} = \sum_{i \ne k} p_{ik}$
    - **Net Change (**$N_k$): $G_k - L_k = A_{2k} - A_{1k}$
    - **Annualized Rate of Change (**$r$): When both class areas are
      positive and $t_2>t_1$, compute the compound rate
      [@puyravaud_standardizing_2003]:
      $$r = \frac{1}{t_2 - t_1} \ln\left(\frac{A_{2k}}{A_{1k}}\right) \times 100\%$$
      Otherwise, report the rate as undefined.

5.  **Top 10 Dominant Transitions Formulation**: To isolate the primary
    landscape change drivers, off-diagonal transitions ($i \ne j$) are
    extracted and sorted descending by area:
    $$\Delta_{total} = \sum_{i \ne j} p_{ij}, \quad \text{Share}_{ij} = \frac{p_{ij}}{\Delta_{total}} \times 100\%$$
    The top 10 transitions are tabulated and exported to show the
    dominant mapped conversion pathways, drawing on the LUMENS Pre-QuES
    approach.

6.  **Spatial Aggregation Scope**: this implementation aggregates the
    mapped transitions over the selected AOI. Planning-unit or
    administrative cross-tabulation is a later extension and requires a
    separate design for zones, overlaps, and area accounting.

::: callout-tip
## Related Function

`change_detection.LULCChangeDetector.compute_spatial_transitions()`:
combines the classified maps, sums pixel area by transition code on the
selected analysis grid, and returns the transition matrix and dynamics
statistics.
:::

## Possible Further Extension: Trajectory Mapping {#sec-manual-trajectory}

Trajectory mapping would let users group observed land-cover transitions
into named categories relevant to their analysis. Users could define the
groups directly or provide a reusable mapping. The system would show the
proposed assignments for review before generating any trajectory
results. The data format, category identifiers, colours, and import
workflow are implementation decisions.

Trajectory mapping remains optional. Without a confirmed mapping, the
change analysis, charts, report, and exports still run. Trajectory maps,
summaries, and report sections are omitted. The system must not infer
policy meanings from class names alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Multi-Epoch Visualization and Analytical Charts {#sec-multitemporal-viz}

Luma-GE prepares the charts in **System Response 8.2: Calculate Mapped
Change**. The user inspects them in **User Journey 8.3: Review Change
and Report**.

This implementation uses simple, readable charts:

1.  **Multi-Epoch Composition:** Stacked bars show each class's mapped
    area or percentage at each available epoch using [Module
    2](@sec-module-2) colours. A stacked area view may be offered for
    three or more comparable epochs; the report must label observation
    dates and must not imply measured change between them.
2.  **Top 10 Transitions:** A horizontal bar chart ranks the ten largest
    off-diagonal class pairs by mapped area in hectares. The
    accompanying table states each pair's share of all mapped change.
3.  **Per-Class Dynamics:** Horizontal bars show gross loss and gross
    gain by class for the selected comparison pair.

Trajectory and interactive flow views are possible further extensions.

::: callout-tip
## Related Function

`dataviz.MultitemporalViz.plot_stacked_composition()`: generates the
stacked composition chart across available project dates.\
`dataviz.MultitemporalViz.plot_top_transitions()`: generates the
horizontal bar chart for the top 10 mapped transitions.
:::

## Generating the Land Use and Land Cover Map Change Analysis Report {#sec-generate-change-report}

This is part of **System Response 8.3: Assemble the Report**. The user
requests and reads the report in **User Journey 8.3: Review Change and
Report**.

The report presents the mapped results, their provenance, and their
limitations in a form users can read and share. Its format and rendering
technology are implementation decisions.

### Tab 1: Single Map Creation and Quality Report Export

Produces the standard single-map quality report for any selected map
identity ($T_i$), adhering to the specifications in [Module
8](@sec-module-8#sec-generate-report): - Report identity block (AOI,
date, sensor). - At a Glance plain-language accuracy summary. -
Comprehensive section-by-section breakdown (Data Acquisition, Scheme,
Sample Data, Separability, Predictors, Model Accuracy, Thematic
Accuracy).

### Tab 2: Land Use and Land Cover Map Change Analysis Report

The report identifies the selected maps, comparison periods, and area of
interest; summarises mapped change with tables and simple charts; and
prominently states the experimental status and limitations described in
@sec-scientific-rigor-change. It shows the relevant source-map
provenance, comparability checks, and validation status supplied by
Modules 1–7 without repeating their detailed methods.

For traceability, each generated report has a visible reference
identifier and a generation date and time with time zone. It identifies
the project, source maps, and analysis version sufficiently to locate
the corresponding run record. The system can retain the associated user
and session context in an access-controlled audit record. These details
help a user find and review an analysis; the visible identifier is not
proof that a shared report has not been altered.

The report is complete without trajectory mapping. A trajectory section
is included only if the optional extension has been run.

::: callout-tip
## Related Function

`report_builder.MultitemporalReportBuilder`: assembles the change
analysis report from the selected maps, results, provenance record, and
limitations.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Asset Export and Housekeeping {#sec-export-change-assets}

The user selects and requests outputs in **User Journey 8.4: Request
Exports**. Luma-GE dispatches the export and returns its status in
**System Response 8.4: Deliver Exports**.

The user can export the change analysis report, summary tables, and
selected map outputs. The system offers an appropriate delivery route
for the size and type of each output and indicates whether an export is
pending, complete, or unsuccessful. Reusable map assets may be saved
when requested. The report and tables remain available even when a
raster requires a separate export task.

Trajectory outputs are included only if the possible further extension
has been run. The specific file formats, service limits, and export
methods are decided during implementation.

## Scope, Caveats, and Possible Further Extension {#sec-scientific-rigor-change}

### Scope of This Implementation

This implementation compares classified maps for selected observation
periods and describes their mapped transitions over a common valid area.
It reports mapped transition areas, class-level dynamics, and simple
visual summaries for exploratory LULC change analysis. A correctly
calculated transition describes a difference between map labels; it does
not by itself verify that land cover changed on the ground. Two selected
periods also cannot establish the precise timing or cause of change, and
this implementation does not determine compliance with any policy or
regulation.

### Experimental Status and Caveats

::: callout-important
This implementation is at a preliminary stage. The trustworthiness of
its mapped transitions depends chiefly on the quality and comparability
of the two input maps. Missing or misclassified pixels, inconsistent
class meanings, differing observation conditions, and spatial
misalignment can appear as change; correct transition arithmetic cannot
remove those problems. The comparison therefore checks and records map
compatibility and the common valid area. Detailed requirements for
imagery, training data, classification, and single-map validation remain
with Modules 1–7.

Reported areas describe mapped categories, not independently verified
change on the ground or error-adjusted estimates of its true area.
Accuracy results for individual maps, when available, must be shown
separately and must not be presented as the accuracy of the change map
[@olofsson_good_2014].

These results should not be used alone for formal quantitative claims or
regulatory decisions. Users are responsible for checking whether the
inputs and methods suit their purpose and for independently verifying
consequential findings. Epistem does not assume responsibility for
decisions or claims made from unverified use of these experimental
outputs.
:::

### Possible Further Extension

- Review selected apparent changes against independent imagery or
  reference information, and report what was checked.
- Use additional observation periods where available to distinguish
  persistent change from short-term variation.
- If a use case requires defensible change accuracy or estimates of
  actual changed area, design an independent reference assessment and
  report uncertainty [@olofsson_good_2014].
